paper.title: Abliteration Is Not a Scalpel: Off-Target Effects of Refusal Removal on Decision Disposition Across Model Families
paper.author: Aleksander Fafuła

design.note: frozen byte-identical prompt; single abliteration author (huihui-ai); weeks-clustered bootstrap CIs

effects.name: optimism
effects.label: Optimism shift (up-bets, pp)
effects.note: abliterated arms bet on the upside more on identical evidence

effects.name: confidence
effects.label: Mean expressed confidence (delta)
effects.note: sign reverses across families; family CIs non-overlapping — 'disinhibition' predicts the wrong pattern

effects.name: confession_length
effects.label: Self-critique verbosity (words)
effects.note: both arms justify longer; length was preregistered as covariate not directional hypothesis

effects.name: horizon
effects.label: Horizon collapse to 1w (share)
effects.note: family-specific: Qwen-abliterated opens the horizon distribution; Gemma stays collapsed in both arms

effects.name: uncertainty_vocabulary
effects.label: Explicit uncertainty words / concessions
effects.both: fewer uncertainty words + more concessive rhetoric in forced self-critiques; stance stability under resampling unchanged in every arm
effects.note: expressed doubt lives in the report, not the behavior

capability_check.note: instruction-following preserved; delta is disposition not capability

contamination_catches: mismatched-quantizer pilot pair produced a publishable-looking artifact overturned by the clean design
stale chat template in a community checkpoint silently mangled the rendered prompt
claims_verified_against: tmp/research/arxiv/2607.17427.md (head findings, tables, and figure captions, lines ~410-530)
simulation_note: Viz is a stylized re-rendering of headline effect sizes — not a reconstruction from raw decisions (not published).
